clue.text: Unemotional sex turns up in novel

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the word for novel

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new or recent

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means the short word for sex is read from bottom to top

parts.note: IT is a long-standing slang word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A novel in which the sex scenes come across as cold and unfeeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns up' reads the slang word for sex upwards, as fits a down clue; 'novel' looks like a book but is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a reserved person who keeps their feelings to themselves seems unemotional.

clue.text: Peel fruit noisily

indicators.note: noisily means the word for the fruit is heard, said out loud, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a pear is a common fruit

explanation.surface: Someone loudly peeling a piece of fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to peel a fruit or vegetable is to strip off its skin with a knife.

clue.text: Indigenous tribe's leader has primitive surroundings

indicators.note: the word for primitive forms surroundings around the tribe's leader

parts.note: primitive art is called naive, simple and untutored

indicators.note: the leader of the tribe is the first letter of that word

explanation.surface: The chief of an indigenous tribe lives amid primitive surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has ... surroundings' puts T, the tribe's first letter, inside NAIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: indigenous people are born in a place, belonging to it from the start.

clue.text: A nice Sun spread provides something offensive

indicators.note: spread means the letters of a nice sun are spread out and laid down in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone complains that even a pleasant spell of sunshine can be irritating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread' rearranges A NICE SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an annoyance or pest is a thing that offends or irritates people.

clue.text: Is sore with gang's violent hostility

indicators.note: violent suggests the letters are thrown about wildly into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word gang as written, the possessive ending giving no letter

explanation.surface: Someone sore over a gang's violent hostility towards them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges IS SORE and GANG.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: belligerent, attacking behaviour is a form of hostility.

clue.text: Iron Duke ended all disheartened, undoubtedly

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its heart, its middle letters, keeping only its outside letters

explanation.surface: The Iron Duke, Wellington, finished his career dispirited, surely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all disheartened' keeps the outside letters of each word: IN, DE and ED. The Iron Duke was the nickname of the Duke of Wellington.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something said to be so beyond doubt is certainly, truly the case.

clue.text: Solitary sailor with parrot capsized in unending ocean

indicators.note: in places the turned sailor and parrot inside the shortened ocean
unending means the last letter of the word for ocean is dropped

parts.note: the sea is the ocean

indicators.note: capsized means the sailor and parrot words are turned over, read backwards

parts.note: a tar is a traditional word for a sailor
to parrot is to ape, copy someone

explanation.surface: A lone sailor and his parrot overturned in the endless ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' gives EPARAT, sailor and parrot read backwards; 'unending' leaves SE; 'in' sets EPARAT between its two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a solitary thing stands apart, alone and detached from others.

clue.text: Unrestrained nude about to show stomach

indicators.note: unrestrained means the letters of nude are set loose and run free in a new order

parts.note: RE is Latin-derived for about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone stripping off without restraint to show off their belly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unrestrained' gives ENDU; 'stomach' looks like the belly but is the verb meaning tolerate.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to stomach something is to put up with it, bear or tolerate it.

clue.text: University fellow accepting reading perhaps is critical

indicators.note: accepting means the university and fellow pieces take the R in between them

parts.note: a gent is a man, a fellow
reading is one of the three Rs of basic education, so it can give R

explanation.surface: A university fellow agreeing that reading is critical.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so 'reading perhaps' gives R; 'accepting' sets it between U and GENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a critical or pressing matter needs immediate attention.

clue.text: Face expressed relief for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means what is heard by listeners, a word that sounds the same

parts.note: someone who sighed let out breath, expressing relief

explanation.surface: An actor breathing out with relief for the benefit of the audience.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a face of a cube or building is one of its flat surfaces.

clue.text: Rash? It's nice and red, sadly

indicators.note: sadly here signals the letters have gone wrong, being badly arranged

parts.note: the letters of the contraction as written

explanation.surface: A skin complaint that sadly looks nice and red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' rearranges ITS, NICE and RED; 'Rash' looks like a skin complaint but means reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a careless, imprudent remark or act is rash, done without thought.

clue.text: Goddess caught in passion by sweetheart

indicators.note: by means next to, so the final letter is set beside the rest
in puts the letter for caught inside the word for passion

parts.note: heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A goddess caught in the throes of passion beside her lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts C inside HEAT; 'sweetheart' is the middle letter of SWEET.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft, magic and crossroads.

clue.text: Desire excessively good helping when going first

indicators.note: going first says the word for when is placed at the front of the other pieces

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
pi is slang for pious, sanctimonious, too good
a ration is a portion, a helping of food

explanation.surface: A wish to be excessively good, helping others before yourself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going first' is not a first-letter signal; it tells you the word for when leads the charade.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an ambition or longing is a strong desire for something.

clue.text: Best spot for view following bell?

definitions.text: Best spot for view following bell?

parts.words: Best spot for view following bell?
parts.note: the bell starts each round of a boxing match, and the closest seats to the boxing ring give the best view of the fight

explanation.surface: Where to stand for the best view after a bell has rung.
explanation.walkthrough: The bell suggests a church or school, but it is the boxer's bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic definition: seats beside the boxing ring are the closest spot for watching a fight.

clue.text: Supports around outside of pole for tents

indicators.note: around says the word for supports wraps round those two letters

parts.note: tees are supports holding golf balls

indicators.note: the outside of the word pole is its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Supports placed around the outside of a pole to hold up tents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' gives PE; 'around' wraps the golf supports round it. Tepee is also spelt teepee or tipi.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: tepees are conical tents of skins or bark used by Native Americans.

clue.text: Body about to be consumed whole

indicators.note: to be consumed means the short word for about is eaten up, taken inside the word for body

parts.note: an entity is a body, a thing that exists as a unit
RE means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A body about to be eaten up whole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be consumed' works on the word for about, not on the body; 'Body' is the start of the wordplay, while 'whole' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the whole of something is all of it, its total.

clue.text: Doctor receiving education in charge of doctor

indicators.note: receiving means the second doctor takes the other pieces into its middle

parts.note: MO is short for medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A doctor getting training from the doctor in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Doctor' is the definition and the second gives the medical officer; 'receiving' splits the medical officer around the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal synonym: medico is jokey slang for a physician or medical student.

clue.text: Cheers after old favourite covering Queen's musical piece

indicators.note: after says the thanks word goes after the other pieces
covering means the favourite wraps around the royal letters

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: A toast following an old favourite song with the Queen's musical piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' gives PERET, the royal cipher inside the favourite; 'after' sends the thanks to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an operetta is a short, light opera with spoken dialogue, a kind of musical work.

clue.text: Rough diamonds in workplace

parts.note: off means unwell, feeling rough
ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: Uncut diamonds hidden somewhere at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough diamonds' looks like one phrase, but the two words give separate pieces, and 'in' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an office is a room or building where people work.

clue.text: Coming back in profit, I repaid drink

indicators.note: Coming back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who has paid back money from their profit goes for a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer lies in 'profit, I repaid' read backwards, signalled by 'Coming back' (the containing 'in' is the link).
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal.

clue.text: Thanksgiving set up supporting first of Pilgrims

indicators.note: in a down clue, supporting means the raising word sits below, holding up the pilgrims letter
first of takes just the opening letter of the word pilgrims

parts.note: to raise is to set up, lift

explanation.surface: The first Thanksgiving, organised with the Pilgrims' help.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'supporting' puts RAISE under P; the Pilgrims are the Plymouth settlers of the first Thanksgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: praise given to God is a form of thanksgiving and worship.

clue.text: After seeing tabloid, comprehension's lowered

indicators.note: after seeing means the comprehension word comes after the tabloid

parts.note: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper
ken is knowledge, understanding, as in beyond my ken

explanation.surface: Reading a tabloid lowers one's grasp of things.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sunken means lowered, set below the level around it.

clue.text: Waterlogged hole covered by turf

indicators.note: in a down clue covered by means the hole sits beneath the turf

parts.note: a sod is a piece of turf
a den is a hole, a lair, a hideaway

explanation.surface: A hole covered by grass, filling with water.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: sodden ground is soaked, saturated with water.

clue.text: Scepticism as term in Dartmoor detains ringleader

indicators.note: detains says the phrase holds the answer within it, the letters kept across the words

explanation.surface: Doubts about a prison sentence at Dartmoor, the prison that holds the gang's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detains' points to MASTERMIND inside 'scepticisM AS TERM IN Dartmoor'. Dartmoor is a well-known prison in Devon.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the brains behind a criminal plot is its mastermind or leader.

clue.text: A behind's endless expanse

indicators.note: endless means the last letter of the word for behind is removed

parts.note: a person's behind is their rear

explanation.surface: Someone's large backside described as a vast expanse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts REAR to REA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an area is a stretch or extent of land or space.

clue.text: Skinny-looking — not good? That's relative

indicators.note: not says the letter for good is removed

parts.note: gaunt means lean and haggard, skinny-looking

explanation.surface: Someone worried that looking skinny is unhealthy, as a relative says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from GAUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a parent's sister is a family member, a relative.

clue.text: Employee seen chaperoning one round town initially?

definitions.text: Employee seen chaperoning one round town initially?

indicators.note: initially takes the opening letter of each of the six words before it

explanation.surface: A paid companion seen taking someone around town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of the six words; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: &lit: a paid escort is a worker hired to accompany a client about town.

clue.text: English bird's wintry, occasionally for ages

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

indicators.note: occasionally takes every other letter of the word wintry

explanation.surface: An English bird finding the weather wintry now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes ITY, the alternate letters of WINTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an eternity is informally a very long time, as in 'it took ages'.
